Article Title: Day 12 of Jharkhand students' protest: Hemant Soren says govt taking exam row 'very seriously'
Article Text:
Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren

NEW DELHI: Jharkhand chief minister Hemant Soren on Wednesday said the state government was treating allegations of irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) with "utmost seriousness and sensitivity," assuring students that justice would be delivered within the constitutional and legal framework.Soren's remarks marked his first public response since students launched protests over alleged paper leaks and irregularities in recruitment examinations."This is a sensitive government that believes in delivering justice. Whenever we take up an issue, we remain committed to resolving it. Our young people will certainly get justice within the ambit of the Constitution and the law," Soren said while speaking to reporters after a programme in Ramgarh district's Nemra village on the first death anniversary of Dishom Guru Shibu Soren."I cannot tear open my chest to show how serious we are, but the government is taking this matter very seriously. This government has eyes, ears and sensitivity. Whatever is appropriate and in the interest of students, the state government will decide accordingly," he added.The chief minister said investigations into the allegations were underway and that the government would take a decision after receiving reports from the agencies probing the matter."We are waiting for the findings and conclusions of the investigating agencies. The people of the state will soon be informed in detail about the matter. Students will receive full support in accordance with constitutional and legal provisions," he said.Soren said the government was closely monitoring developments and that administrative processes were continuing at all levels. He added that the probe agencies were actively investigating the allegations and that the government's final decision would be announced after all facts and findings were available.Meanwhile, students protesting at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium in Ranchi entered the 12th day of their agitation on Wednesday. They are demanding cancellation of the 14th JPSC Combined Civil Services Preliminary Examination, a CBI and ED probe into alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC recruitment examinations, disclosure of OMR sheets, main examination answer scripts and category-wise cut-off marks, blacklisting of controversial examination agencies, and comprehensive reforms in the state's recruitment bodies.
Article Summary: Jharkhand chief minister Hemant Soren said the state government was treating allegations of irregularities with "utmost seriousness and sensitivity" Soren's remarks marked his first public response since students launched protests over alleged paper leaks and irregularities in recruitment examinations. The chief minister said investigations into the allegations were underway.

NEW DELHI: Indian cargo ship MSV Faize Noore Oliya was hit by a projectile in Red Sea off Yemen Tuesday, causing the vessel to capsize and sink, shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal said, adding all 14 seafarers, including 13 Indian nationals, have been rescued.India condemned this "unprovoked attack on the defenceless mechanised sailing vessel" and said continuing incidents of attacks on commercial shipping in the region are deeply worrisome. Article Title: Stalker uses husband's name to lure teacher to school gate, stabs her 20 times in Faridabad
Article Text:
Footage shows accused lunge at Sandhya the moment she reaches the classroom entrance, and pull her to the corridor

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think should be done to better prevent stalking-related crimes? Stricter laws against stalking Faster action on complaints More public awareness campaigns 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





GURGAON: A stalker who allegedly pursued a 26-year-old teacher for nearly two years walked into a private school in Faridabad on Monday morning, tricked her into coming to the main gate by using her husband’s name, and then stabbed her more than 20 times in a vicious attack in front of staff and students until the blade bent.Captured on CCTV cameras, the attack unfolded in seconds and left the young English teacher dead before she could be taken to hospital.The accused, Amit (21), a resident of Kot village in Faridabad, was arrested within a couple of hours. Police said he had been stalking Sandhya, who taught at Saraswati Senior Secondary School in Sikrona, and attacked her after she allegedly severed all contact with him and warned him she would approach police if he continued to harass her.Amit entered the school around 9.30am, his face partially covered with a scarf, and asked staff to inform Sandhya that “Vicky” had come to meet her, referring to her husband. Believing her husband was waiting outside, she walked towards the entrance.Footage shows him lunge at Sandhya the moment she reaches the classroom entrance, and pull her to the corridor. Amit punches her as she cries out for help, pulls out a knife in a flash and goes on a stabbing fit, puncturing her neck, abdomen and upper body several times as she slumps to the ground.School principal Tejpal is seen rushing into the corridor to rescue Sandhya after hearing her screams but is forced to step back as the attacker threatens him with the knife.“There were students inside the school and Sandhya was taking classes. He used her husband’s name to call her outside. No sooner did he reach the gate, he attacked her. He stabbed her over 20 times. When I tried to stop him, he threatened to attack me too. We rushed her to Al-Falah Medical College, where she was declared dead on arrival,” the principal told TOI.Police sources said Amit had allegedly bought the knife around two months ago and is suspected to have been planning the murder since then. While the exact number of stab wounds will be confirmed after the autopsy, CCTV footage showed him stabbing Sandhya about 20 times in just 13 seconds. Amit had come to the school on a motorcycle.Sandhya, who had a love marriage with Vikas, is survived by their two children — a five-year-old son and a three-year-old daughter. The attack triggered panic on the campus. Teachers quickly moved frightened children back into classrooms while parents began arriving after news spread. Police cordoned off the school as forensic teams collected evidence.Based on a complaint by Sandhya’s husband, a case was registered under Section 103(1) (murder) of BNS at Sector 58 police station.Police spokesperson Yashpal Yadav said the anti-vehicle theft squad and a team from Sikrona police station tracked down Amit within two hours.“During questioning, the accused said he knew Sandhya from the school in his village where she earlier taught. She later stopped speaking to him and warned of legal action if he continued following her,” Yadav added.Police said the accused will be produced before a local court and his custody sought for further interrogation. CCTV footage and other evidence are being examined as part of the probe, they added.
Article Summary: A stalker walked into a private school in Faridabad on Monday morning, tricked her into coming to the main gate by using her husband’s name. He then stabbed her more than 20 times in a vicious attack in front of staff and students until the blade bent. The accused, Amit (21), a resident of Kot village infaridabad, was arrested within a couple of hours.

Article Title: 'Arrest Abhijeet Dipke immediately': Social media influencer files complaint against CJP founder
Article Text:
Ansari alleged that men associated with Abhijeet Dipke attacked him and urged the police to arrest Dipke immediately.





NEW DELHI: Social media influencer Faizan Ansari on Tuesday said he has filed a written complaint with the Delhi Police against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke, alleging that men linked to the party attacked him in Maharashtra.Ansari claimed he has evidence to support his allegations and urged the police to arrest Dipke immediately."Today, I have filed a written complaint against Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of the CJP party, with the Delhi DCP, because I have proof that his men attacked me. I was attacked in Pune and in Aurangabad. There are already 2 cases filed on that, " Ansari told ANI.He also praised the Delhi government and police for detaining activist Sonam Wangchuk during the recent protests, claiming the move prevented the law and order situation in the national capital from worsening."I want the Delhi police to immediately arrest Dipke. Moreover, I salute the Delhi CM and the police for detaining Sonam Wangchuk at the right time, due to which the atmosphere in Delhi was saved from deteriorating. Dipke is doing everything for his own benefit, " Ansari added“Moreover, I salute the Delhi CM and the police for detaining Sonam Wangchuk at the right time, due to which the atmosphere in Delhi was saved from deteriorating.Dipke is doing everything for his own benefit,” Ansari alleged.Earlier on Monday, Dipke had rejected comparisons between the CJP-led protests over alleged recruitment and examination irregularities and anti-government movements in Bangladesh and Nepal, saying Indian protesters draw inspiration from Mahatma Gandhi's legacy of peaceful resistance.Dipke also spoke about the CJP's expansion plans, compensation for the families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide, and the state of education in India.Dipke also dismissed exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen's remarks comparing the CJP's protest in Delhi against exam irregularities with the 2024 movement that led to the ouster of former Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina's Awami League government.“Protests in Bangladesh, Nepal are being used to defame us; we are different," he asserted.“We showed during the recent protest in Delhi that we were following the Constitution and holding our demonstration peacefully. Parallels to the protests in Bangladesh and Nepal are being used to defame us.“We don’t need to look at Bangladesh or Nepal when we have Mahatma Gandhi from whom the world takes inspiration to protest,” Dipke said.People are drawing comparisons with the protests in Bangladesh and Nepal because the alleged police brutality reminded them of scenes from those countries, he said.“The students in India were not violent or aggressive. They got their heads, arms and legs broken but displayed restraint and sat peacefully at Jantar Mantar," Dipke said.
Article Summary: Social media influencer Faizan Ansari on Tuesday said he has filed a written complaint with the Delhi Police against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke. Ansari claimed he has evidence to support his allegations and urged the police to arrest Dipke immediately. He also praised the Delhi government and police for detaining activist Sonam Wangchuk.

Article Title: Over 30 operatives killed by 'Indian agents' since 2020: LeT commander
Article Text:
Rizwan Hanif, a commander affiliated with Lashkar-e-Taiba, has alleged that Indian agents have systematically killed more than thirty individuals in different Pakistani locations since 2020. He characterized these murders as acts of religious persecution and rejected the authority of foreign entities. This statement comes amid heightened rhetoric from Pakistan's military, and experts suggest it serves as a strategic narrative amidst rising tensions.

In a significant public admission by terrorist organisation Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), senior commander Rizwan Hanif has claimed that over 30 members linked to the group have been killed across Pakistani cities since 2020 by "India agents". LeT members were targeted in Peshawar, Karachi, Rawalpindi, Muzaffarabad and Rawalakot, Hanif said while addressing a crowd in Pakistan.Attempting to frame these targeted killings as religious persecution, Hanif - the wanted deputy chief of Lashkar's POK unit - launched into inflammatory rhetoric. In a video circulated on social media, he questioned the group's "crime", asserting they were targeted solely for their faith.Hanif also launched a sharp attack against other faiths in his speech which was filmed by his followers and uploaded on social media.He declared that the outfit would continue its activities, rejecting the authority of foreign powers, including the US and Israel.The hate-filled speech comes on the heels of Lt General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, the official spokesperson of Pakistan armed forces (DG-ISPR), and the son of a US-designated terrorist peddling similar extremist views on a video while alleging that Afghans were not Muslims.Security experts saw these speeches as a face-saving narrative building exercise. The escalation in sectarian rhetoric comes as Islamabad faces mounting public unrest in Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir, where violent state crackdowns against anti-govt protesters at Rawalakot, in particular, and other places have drawn severe criticism while denting Pakistan's narrative about it being the champion of Kashmiris and their right to self-determination.Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif also labelled anti-govt demonstrators in POK as "enemies" comparable to India and ruled out any dialogue with them while defending the violent attacks on protesters.
Article Summary: Rizwan Hanif, a commander affiliated with Lashkar-e-Taiba, has alleged that Indian agents have systematically killed more than thirty individuals in different Pakistani locations since 2020. He characterized these murders as acts of religious persecution and rejected the authority of foreign entities. This statement comes amid heightened rhetoric from Pakistan's military, and experts suggest it serves as a strategic narrative.

Article Title: Indian cargo vessel sinks after attack in Yemeni waters; all 14 crew rescued
Article Text:
A projectile attack sank the Indian-flagged vessel off Yemen, but all 14 crew members, including 13 Indians, were safely rescued. (Representational image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: An Indian-flagged cargo vessel was struck by a projectile and sank off Yemen’s western coast on Tuesday. All 14 crew members aboard the vessel were rescued and brought to safety.Union minister for ports, shipping and waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, said the MSV Faize Noore Oliya was hit by a projectile in Yemeni waters, causing it to capsize and sink. The crew comprised 13 Indian nationals and one Yemeni sailor.The Yemeni Coast Guard rescued all 14 crew members and brought them safely to the port of Mokha, Sonowal added. No casualties were reported.Ministry of External Affairs said the vessel sank in the Red Sea off the Yemeni coast on August 4 and confirmed that all 13 Indian nationals had been rescued. The Indian Embassy in Riyadh was coordinating with Yemeni authorities to ensure the safety of the crew and provide necessary assistance.The government-affiliated National Resistance Forces said coast guard and naval units carried out a joint rescue operation after the vessel was attacked about 13 nautical miles (24 km) south of the Houthi-held port city of Hodeidah.The National Resistance Forces blamed Yemen’s Houthi rebels for the attack.The Houthis have not commented on the incident.Sonowal condemned what he called an “unprovoked attack” and said the safety of Indian seafarers remained the government’s “supreme priority”. He said the Director General of Maritime Administration had been instructed to coordinate with relevant agencies to ensure the security of Indian sailors in the region.The MEA also expressed concern over continued attacks on commercial shipping in the region, saying such targeting “must end”. It called for free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through international waterways in the region, in accordance with international law, to be restored at the earliest.
Article Summary: The MSV Faize Noore Oliya was hit by a projectile in Yemeni waters, causing it to capsize and sink. The Yemeni Coast Guard rescued all 14 crew members and brought them safely to the port of Mokha. No casualties were reported.

Article Title: Udhayanidhi: Udhayanidhi Stalin arrest drama: 'No double meaning in my speech; TN CM using diversion tactic,' says DMK leader - top developments
Article Text:
Udhayanidhi acknowledged the crowd, waving and greeting supporters before leaving the premises

Udhayanidhi says 'false cases won't stop me', denies double-meaning remark

Udhayanidhi leaves police station after questioning, greeted by cheering DMK workers

High Court orders release after questioning

Arrested over alleged remarks linked to Trisha

Udhayanidhi denies allegations, says remarks were distorted

DMK alleges political vendetta; Stalin attacks TVK government

EPS calls Udhayanidhi's remarks condemnable, questions timing of arrest

Protests erupt across Tamil Nadu

TVK, Opposition leaders condemn remarks

NEW DELHI: DMK leader and leader of opposition in the Tamil Nadu Assembly Udhayanidhi Stalin was arrested on Tuesday over his alleged "double-meaning" remark linked to actor Trisha.While the Madras high court directed that he would be released on station bail after questioning, the day witnessed dramatic political developments, protests by DMK workers and a war of words between the ruling TVK government and the opposition.Addressing supporters after being released from Sengipatti Police Station, Udhayanidhi dismissed the case against him as politically motivated and accused the ruling TVK of using "diversion tactics and fake news".He maintained that his speech at the Thanjavur farmers' protest contained no double meaning and was intended only to demand Cauvery water for farmers."I don't have any intention to malign anyone. My parents did not nurture me that way. I have a family and a sister," he said. Thanking DMK cadres, senior leaders and the party's legal wing for standing by him, Udhayanidhi added that "foisting false cases will not stop me" and said he would continue raising farmers' issues.He also expressed disappointment that some political leaders criticised him without watching his full speech.Udhayanidhi Stalin walked out of the Sengipatti Police Station in Thanjavur after being questioned in connection with a case over his alleged remarks during a public meeting.As he emerged from the police station, the DMK leader was greeted by a large gathering of party cadres, who raised slogans in his support.Udhayanidhi acknowledged the crowd, waving and greeting supporters before leaving the premises.He had been detained earlier in the day and brought from Chennai for questioning.Also read| After arrest and 90-minute grilling, Udhayanidhi Stalin released by Thanjavur police The Madras high court had directed the police to release him after completing the inquiry and asked him to cooperate with the investigation whenever required.Questioning of Udhayanidhi Stalin began at the Sengipatti police station in Thanjavur district. After stepping out of the police vehicle that brought him from Chennai, the DMK leader waved at the large gathering of supporters outside before entering the police station for the inquiry.DMK cadres continued to assemble outside the premises, raising slogans in his support.After a brief delay, Udhayanidhi Stalin stepped out of the police van that brought him from Chennai and entered the Sengipatti police station in Thanjavur district for questioning.Meanwhile, DMK cadres have also started gathering in large numbers outside the police station, raising slogans in support of the leader of opposition as the inquiry gets underway.In the latest development, police changed the venue for Udhayanidhi Stalin's questioning, rerouting his convoy to Sengipatti between Thanjavur and Tiruchirappalli instead of the Thanjavur West police station, where he was initially expected to be questioned.Former DMK ministers K N Nehru, E V Velu and M R K Panneerselvam reached the Sengipatti police station and accompanied Udhayanidhi during the inquiry.Meanwhile, a large number of DMK cadres gathered near the Thanjavur West police station after reports initially suggested that he would be questioned there.Earlier in the day, the Madras high court directed the Tamil Nadu Police to release Udhayanidhi after completing the inquiry and asked him to cooperate with the investigation whenever required.During the hearing, advocate general Vijay Narayan informed the court that the police did not intend to seek Udhayanidhi's judicial remand."He has already been arrested but will be let off after questioning. We do not intend to remand Udhayanidhi Stalin. He will be released on station bail after inquiry," the advocate general told the court, according to news agency ANI.Udhayanidhi was taken into custody by the Thanjavur Police from his residence in Chennai's Neelankarai on Tuesday morning in connection with an FIR registered over his speech at a Cauvery protest in Thanjavur on Monday.He has been booked under multiple provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act and the Information Technology Act.Also read| Smiles, waves and slogans: How Udhayanidhi’s arrest turned into a political spectacle Charges include allegedly using obscene words, insulting the modesty of a woman, promoting enmity, provoking riots and criminal intimidation.The controversy erupted after sections of the crowd chanted actor Trisha's name during his speech, following which he allegedly made a double-entendre remark.The women's wing of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) lodged a complaint, alleging that the remarks insulted the actor and women in general.Before being taken away by the police, Udhayanidhi maintained that he had not targeted anyone and said the matter would be decided by the courts."Did I mention anyone's name except the CM's? Then why do you think this is happening? Let the court decide," he told reporters.Later, he alleged that edited clips of his speech had been circulated to create a "fake narrative.""They have propagated fake news by using 'Cut, Copy, Paste' to claim I said something I never said. I am not the kind of person to be intimidated by all this. I will face it legally," he said, as quoted by ANI.The DMK has maintained that his remarks were misrepresented and were directed at the government's functioning rather than any individual.DMK president M K Stalin strongly criticised the TVK government over the arrest, accusing it of acting with "arrogance" and trying to stop Udhayanidhi from attending the Assembly budget session.Also read| 'Reel creator instead of CM': Stalin attacks Vijay over Udhayanidhi's arrest He alleged that police had "arrogantly" taken Udhayanidhi into custody from Chennai and transported him to Thanjavur under non-bailable charges. Stalin also claimed that the government's stand changed in court after public outrage, with its lawyers stating there was no intention to seek judicial custody.Calling the high court's order a setback for the government, Stalin demanded the immediate release of all DMK workers detained during protests across the state.AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami (EPS), criticised both Udhayanidhi Stalin's alleged remarks and the Vijay government's decision to arrest him ahead of the Assembly's budget session.In a post on X, EPS said Udhayanidhi's "degrading remarks about women" were "strongly condemnable" and claimed he had repeatedly said the DMK leader "needs a muzzle."However, he also questioned the timing of the arrest, alleging it appeared politically motivated and aimed at paralysing the Assembly by preventing the leader of the opposition from attending the session.EPS urged the government to withdraw the arrest action immediately.The arrest triggered protests by DMK cadres across Tamil Nadu, with workers staging demonstrations and road blockades condemning the police action.At the party headquarters, M K Stalin chaired a meeting to discuss the next course of action ahead of the Assembly session beginning on August 5.Senior leaders, including P K Sekar Babu, K N Nehru and Ma Subramanian, rallied behind Udhayanidhi, while the party moved the Madras High Court seeking anticipatory bail before his arrest.While the DMK defended Udhayanidhi, the ruling TVK intensified its attack.TVK spokesperson Americai Narayanan accused the DMK leader of insulting women during a protest meant to highlight farmers' issues, claiming that people had begun referring to him as "vulgar nidhi".Congress MP Jothimani also criticised Udhayanidhi, saying women should not be dragged into political battles and describing the remarks as "objectionable."The TVK has filed complaints with both the Thanjavur Police and the National Commission for Women, seeking action and an unconditional public apology from Udhayanidhi.Tamil Nadu electricity minister R Nirmal Kumar questioned Udhayanidhi's suitability for public office following the controversy.
Article Summary: DMK leader and leader of opposition in the Tamil Nadu Assembly Udhayanidhi Stalin was arrested on Tuesday over his alleged "double-meaning" remark linked to actor Trisha. The Madras high court directed the police to release him after completing the inquiry and asked him to cooperate with the investigation whenever required.

Article Title: 'Will do whatever is necessary for national interest': India after Pakistan deploys 250 Chinese Howitzers
Article Text:
File photo: Chinese self-propelled artillery guns

Pakistan deploys Chinese SH-15 howitzers

India also modernising artillery

NEW DELHI: India on Tuesday said it would do "whatever is necessary" to safeguard its national interests after reports emerged that Pakistan had deployed a large number of Chinese-made SH-15 self-propelled artillery guns along the border facing India.Responding to a question during the ministry of external affairs' weekly media briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India's position remained unchanged on cross-border terrorism and asserted that the country would remain prepared to defend itself."During Operation Sindoor, we saw how a befitting reply was given (to Pakistan). From our side, our stance is that cross-border terrorism must stop, and we will do whatever is necessary in our national interest, for which we always remain vigilantly deployed," Jaiswal said.The remarks came a day after reports said Pakistan had deployed around 250 Chinese-origin SH-15 wheeled self-propelled howitzers in formations facing India as part of its artillery modernisation programme.In the briefing, Jaiswal also strongly criticised the recently held elections in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoK), describing them as a "complete farce" and accusing Pakistan of using force to suppress public dissent."This so-called local election in PoK is a complete farce. The real happening is that of public protests and wanton killings by Pakistani forces. Such hollow exercises cannot hide reality," Jaiswal said.He said that at least 90 civilians had been killed since June during the crackdown in PoK."Since June this year, at least 90 civilians have lost their lives in the continuing crackdown. The Pakistani Establishment has answered public discontent with bullets, blackouts, intimidation and repression, and now seeks to manufacture legitimacy through a hollow electoral exercise," he said, urging the international community to hold Islamabad accountable.Jaiswal also responded to a media inquiry about a viral video in which members of the Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba claimed that 30 to 40 of their commanders had been killed, alleging that Indian agencies were responsible for the killings.He said, "We continue to call upon all countries to take strong action against cross-border terrorism and those who promote it. We also call upon Pakistan to take decisive action against cross-border terrorism and dismantle the terrorist infrastructure operating from its soil."Pakistan ordered 236 SH-15 155mm/52-calibre wheeled self-propelled artillery guns from Chinese state-owned defence firm Norinco in 2019, with deliveries beginning in 2022 and a second batch arriving in 2023.Pakistan has also acquired a transfer of technology agreement to manufacture the artillery system at Heavy Industries Taxila.The SH-15, known as the PCL-181 in China, has reportedly been deployed mainly in Pakistan's Gujranwala, Sialkot and Jalalpur Jattan sectors opposite India, particularly around the Shakargarh Bulge.The guns were also used during Operation Sindoor.The 155mm artillery system is capable of firing multiple types of ammunition and has a range of more than 50 kilometres when using rocket-assisted projectiles.Retired Lieutenant General PR Shankar, former Director General of Artillery, told TOI that the acquisition strengthens Pakistan's conventional firepower and complements its Army Rocket Force, enhancing its long-range strike capabilities.The deployment comes as India continues to modernise its own artillery under the Field Artillery Rationalisation Plan.The Indian Army has inducted 155mm artillery systems such as the M777 ultra-light howitzer, the K-9 Vajra self-propelled gun and the indigenous Dhanush gun. It has also placed orders for 307 Advanced Towed Artillery Gun Systems (ATAGS), developed domestically.India is also working on a wheeled Mounted Gun System (MGS), based on the ATAGS platform, which is currently in the advanced stages of development and has undergone initial firing trials.
Article Summary: India says it will do "whatever is necessary" to safeguard its national interests. India's position remains unchanged on cross-border terrorism, says MEA spokesperson. Pakistan has deployed 250 Chinese-origin SH-15 wheeled self- propelled howitzers in formations facing India.

Article Title: Terror suspects spotted, search ops launched in J&K’s Poonch
Article Text:
Following intelligence indicating potential terror suspects in Poonch, security forces have launched coordinated operations in two strategic locations. Reports have confirmed sightings near Gujjar Naar and Kherowali dhok, prompting a thorough search in the isolated Dhara Sangla village by army and police units. As of Tuesday evening, no contact with the suspects has been reported. Earlier, a significant search initiative was executed in the Thanamandi area of Rajouri district.

JAMMU: Security forces on Tuesday initiated joint cordon-and-search operations in two locations in J&K’s Poonch district after being alerted about the alleged movement of terror suspects.According to intelligence inputs, three terror suspects were seen near Gujjar Naar area, and four more were spotted close to Kherowali dhok (high-altitude temporary huts constructed by nomads) in the remote Dhara Sangla village in Surankote sector.Troops of the Army’s 16 Rashtriya Rifles and J&K Police’s Special Operations Group subsequently launched intensive searches. No contact was established with the terror suspects till Tuesday evening, even as both operations remained underway, officials said.Earlier on July 14, a massive combing operation was carried out across multiple villages in Rajouri district’s Thanamandi after CCTV footage purportedly captured the movement of two terror suspects in the area.
Article Summary: Security forces have launched coordinated operations in two strategic locations. Reports have confirmed sightings near Gujjar Naar and Kherowali dhok, prompting a thorough search in the isolated Dhara Sangla village by army and police units. As of Tuesday evening, no contact with the suspects has been reported.

Article Title: NC, PDP announce protest plans; BJP to celebrate Article 370 abrogation
Article Text:
Kashmir's political landscape will witness separate protests from the NC and PDP this Wednesday, marking seven years since Article 370 was abrogated. The NC is pushing for the restoration of its statehood, whereas the PDP demands the reinstatement of Article 370. Meanwhile, BJP's celebratory events, including a Tiranga rally from Lal Chowk, suggest a contrasting narrative on the changes in Jammu and Kashmir's sentiments following the abrogation.

SRINAGAR: NC and PDP announced plans for separate protests on Wednesday on the seventh anniversary of the abrogation of Article 370 and bifurcation of erstwhile J&K into two Union territories. BJP said it would mark the day with celebratory events at its party headquarters and in districts.J&K’s governing NC said it would hold peaceful protests to demand the restoration of statehood while PDP said its demonstrations would seek the restoration of Article 370 and the release of political prisoners.“On this day, I would just say they (Centre) should fulfil their promise. They promised the people of J&K and the entire country that statehood would be restored after elections and delimitation. Both have been done,” NC chief Farooq Abdullah said.BJP spokesperson Sajid Yousuf Shah said the party would take out a Tiranga rally from Lal Chowk, adding the abrogation of Article 370 had changed the mood in J&K.
Article Summary: NC and PDP announce plans for separate protests on the seventh anniversary of the abrogation of Article 370 and bifurcation of erstwhile J&K into two Union territories. BJP said it would mark the day with celebratory events at its party headquarters and in districts.

Article Title: ‘Will give fitting reply at appropriate time’: Sunetra Pawar on Congress’ ‘gungi gudiya’ jibe

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra deputy chief minister and NCP president Sunetra Pawar on Tuesday said she would give a "fitting reply" at an "appropriate time" after the Congress' state unit called her a "gungi gudiya" (mute/silent doll).“When the time comes, I will give a fitting reply,” Sunetra Pawar told reporters when asked about the Congress’ criticism.Her response came amid a political row triggered by a social media post by the Maharashtra Congress referring to her as a “gungi gudiya”, drawing sharp criticism from the NCP and its ruling alliance partners, the BJP and the Shiv Sena.NCP leaders, including the party’s working president Praful Patel, condemned the remark as “derogatory and disrespectful” towards a woman leader.In a statement, Patel called the language used against Sunetra Pawar “insulting.”“Maharashtra, which follows the progressive ideals of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj, Mahatma Jyotiba Phule, B.R. Ambedkar and Yashwantrao Chavan, will never accept the insult of women. It is unfortunate and condemnable that the Congress has used such language against a woman leader despite the party being led by women leaders such as Sonia Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi,” the former Union minister added.Patel demanded that the Congress immediately delete the post and issue a public apology.The controversy escalated after a group of NCP workers entered the Congress’ Gandhi Bhavan office in Mumbai and staged a protest over the post.Maharashtra Congress president Harshwardhan Sapkal condemned the NCP workers’ action, alleging that the protesters intended to resort to violence and accusing the BJP and the police of backing them.He, however, maintained that the Congress would continue to follow Mahatma Gandhi’s path of non-violence despite the provocation.Sunetra Pawar took over as Maharashtra deputy chief minister following the death of her husband, Ajit Pawar, in a plane crash in January. The following month, she became the NCP president, filling the vacancy created by his demise.
Article Summary: NCP president Sunetra Pawar says she will give a "fitting reply" at an "appropriate time" Her response comes amid a political row triggered by a social media post by the Maharashtra Congress referring to her as a "gungi gudiya"

Article Title: Security on high alert in Jammu & Kashmir: Pakistani drone sighted in Kathua, anti-terror search intensifies in Poonch
Article Text:
File photo: Security forces intensify search operations in Poonch

Massive anti-terror search underway in Poonch

Unexploded mortar shell recovered near border

Comes amid heightened tensions along India-Pakistan border

Similar drone sightings reported recently

NEW DELHI: Security forces on Tuesday launched a search operation after a Pakistani drone was spotted hovering over forward villages along the International Border in Jammu and Kashmir's Kathua district.The development comes amid heightened security concerns along the border following reports of Pakistan strengthening its military deployment opposite India.The drone intruded into Indian territory around 2 pm and was seen hovering over the forward villages of Shukhmal, Devindera and Tapan in the Bobiyan area of Kathua's Hiranagar sector.Alert Border Security Force (BSF) personnel immediately initiated countermeasures to bring down the drone.However, the flying object, which was at a high altitude, managed to return across the border before it could be intercepted.Following the incident, the BSF and Jammu and Kashmir Police launched an extensive search operation to ensure that the drone had not dropped any weapons, explosives or other material.The operation was continuing at the time of the last reports, according to news agency PTI.Separately, security forces also launched a large-scale cordon-and-search operation across dozens of remote villages in Poonch district following intelligence inputs about the suspected movement of two groups of terrorists.Personnel from the Special Operations Group (SOG) of the Jammu and Kashmir Police, assisted by the Rashtriya Rifles, carried out searches in villages including Dhara Sangla, Gujjar Naar and Kherowali Dhok in Surankote tehsil.Officials said no contact had yet been established with the suspected terrorists, while systematic searches were continuing in the densely forested region.Security personnel also searched Kalaban and adjoining areas in Mendhar tehsil, but no arrests were made.In another security-related development, an old rusted mortar shell was recovered from the courtyard of a house in Kattal-Brahmana village in Kathua's Hiranagar sector on Tuesday morning.Labourers carrying out excavation work at the residence noticed the suspicious object and informed the authorities. A police team, along with the Bomb Disposal Squad (BDS), secured the area and safely removed the unexploded shell for disposal.The recent drone intrusion occurs during a time of heightened tension along the border. Earlier today, India said it would do "whatever is necessary" to safeguard its national interests following reports that Pakistan had deployed around 250 Chinese-origin SH-15 self-propelled artillery guns along sectors facing India.Responding to the reports during the ministry of external affairs' weekly briefing on Tuesday, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, "During Operation Sindoor, we saw how a befitting reply was given (to Pakistan). From our side, our stance is that cross-border terrorism must stop, and we will do whatever is necessary in our national interest, for which we always remain vigilantly deployed."The Chinese-made SH-15 155mm/52-calibre artillery systems have been deployed primarily in Pakistan's Gujranwala, Sialkot and Jalalpur Jattan sectors opposite India as part of Islamabad's artillery modernisation programme.The latest incident follows another suspected Pakistani drone sighting reported in Rajouri district last month. Blinking lights were seen over forward villages in the Sunderbani sector before the suspected unmanned aerial vehicle returned towards Pakistan.Security forces had subsequently conducted a search operation to check for any airdropped payload but found nothing suspicious.Earlier in June, Army personnel had also opened fire after spotting a Pakistani drone over forward posts in the Balakote sector of Poonch, forcing it to retreat towards Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.
Article Summary: Pakistani drone spotted hovering over forward villages along the International Border in Jammu and Kashmir's Kathua district. Security forces launch extensive search operation to ensure drone had not dropped weapons, explosives or other material. Separately, security forces also launch large-scale cordon-and-search operation across dozens of remote villages in Poonch district.

NEW DELHI: The Ministry of External Affairs on Tuesday slammed the recently conducted so-called local elections in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoK), calling them “a complete farce” and accusing Pakistani forces of using violence, blackouts, intimidation and repression against civilians.Addressing a media briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, “The real happening is that of public protests and wanton killings by Pakistani forces. Article Title: RTI queries his US degree; CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke counters, asks 'emperor' to show his
Article Text: CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke on Monday hit back at questions over his US education, saying he was ready to publicly produce documents relating to his scholarship and education loan while challenging the “emperor” to reveal his own academic credentials.The response came after Surat-based activist Amit Tiwari filed RTI applications seeking details on how Dipke funded his studies at the Boston University despite coming from a modest family background. Dipke’s father is a retired junior engineer.Without naming anyone, Dipke said, “I came to know that some BJP worker has filed RTI applications against me and he wants to know how I completed my education. So, I would like to ask him whether the ‘emperor’ will show his degree? I am ready to show my scholarship letter and loan letter.”In a social media post, Dipke also repeated the challenge, asking: “Will the emperor show his degree?”The 30-year-old student activist, who is currently at his home in Waluj after concluding his 36-day agitation at Jantar Mantar that ended with the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, questioned why his academic journey was under scrutiny.“I don’t understand why these people are so against education,” Dipke said, adding that some people appeared uncomfortable with a person from his background pursuing higher education in US.Meanwhile, CJP announced that its top leadership will hold a two-day strategy meeting in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar from Aug 5 to chart the organisation’s future course following its recent agitation.“Over the past several days, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) team members have consulted a wide range of stakeholders on what its next steps should be, including a team of 50 core volunteers who dedicated their time and effort throughout the Jantar Mantar protest,” the organisation said in a statement quoting chief spokesperson Saurav Das.CJP said it would subsequently launch a nationwide tour to listen to and engage with young people across the country.“In the days following the strategy meet, CJP will reach out to its volunteers across the country and organise a nationwide listening tour to take into account the youths’ needs and aspirations,” the statement said.CJP functionaries said further details regarding the tour and the organisation’s future roadmap would be announced in the coming days.
Article Summary: Abhijeet Dipke says he is ready to publicly produce documents relating to his scholarship and education loan. The response came after Surat-based activist Amit Tiwari filed RTI applications seeking details on how Dipke funded his studies at the Boston University.

NEW DELHI: A CRPF officer allegedly shot dead two of his colleagues and injured another before killing himself at a camp in Assam's Nagaon district on Tuesday, police told news agency PTI.The incident took place at the CRPF's 34 Battalion camp in Katimari, Nagaon, at around 7 am, when Assistant Sub-Inspector (GD) Ballani Premabaram, who was on duty at the main gate, allegedly opened fire on his colleagues, Nagaon Deputy Superintendent of Police (HQ) Paramita Sarkar told PTI.Premabaram later turned the weapon on himself and died at the spot, she said.Head Constable (GD) Vishnu Prasad Baghel and Sub-Inspector (GD) Ramnawal Singh Yadav were killed in the firing, while Assistant Sub-Inspector (Mane) Govind Sripul was injured and admitted to a private hospital for treatment.

Article Title: 'Resignations are part of politics': DKS on two Congress MLAs quitting over Karnataka cabinet snub

NEW DELHI: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar on Tuesday downplayed the resignation of two Congress MLAs who quit the legislative assembly after being left out of the state cabinet expansion, saying "it is a part of politics. "Shivakumar said, "Resignations are a part of politics. No one can stop those who want to resign. If they want the party and a political future, they should stay."Drawing from his own political journey, the chief minister said he too had been denied ministerial berths in the past but chose to remain with the party."If there is a party, everything else follows. When I was denied a ministerial berth during the tenures of Dharam Singh and Siddaramaiah, I could have resigned too. Didn't G Parameshwara and I remain patient?" he said.Shivakumar also said he had directed all ministers to immediately visit their respective districts to assess the drought relief situation.The remarks came a day after Congress MLAs Yashavantarayagouda V Patil (Indi) and Belur Gopalakrishna (Sagar) resigned from the Karnataka Legislative Assembly, expressing disappointment over being excluded from the cabinet expansion.Patil submitted his resignation to Deputy Speaker Rudrappa Lamani at the Vidhana Soudha. Soon after, his supporters staged a protest in Bengaluru, alleging that he had been treated unfairly by the party.Gopalakrishna also resigned, adding to the pressure on the Congress leadership ahead of the swearing-in ceremony for the new ministers.Speaking to reporters, Patil claimed his name had been included in the list of ministers until the last moment but was dropped from the final announcement."I have been watching the developments within the party; ultimately today, during the expansion, our leadership failed to keep the promise made. The situation in Vijayapura district is that loyalty and honesty are not valued in the Congress party . I have no other choice. Article Title: Bankipur bypoll: BJP chief Nitin Nabin vows introspection after Kishor ends party's 30-yr hold
Article Text:
Nitin Nabin says BJP will introspect after losing Bankipur bypoll to Prashant Kishor

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Monday said the party would undertake a "thorough introspection" after losing the Bankipur Assembly bypoll in Bihar, where Jan Suraaj founder Prashant Kishor defeated BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar to end the party's three-decade dominance in the constituency.Kishor won the bypoll by 19,324 votes, polling 64,151 votes against Neeraj Kumar's 44,827 votes. The victory marked Kishor's first electoral win since launching the Jan Suraaj Party and came less than a year after the party failed to win a single seat in the 2025 Bihar Assembly elections.Reacting to the bypoll results, Nabin accepted the verdict and said the BJP would analyse the reasons behind its defeats.In a post on X, Nabin said, "We accept the mandate received in today's three assembly by-elections.We express our heartfelt gratitude to the people of Manjalpur assembly constituency in Gujarat for expressing their faith in the Bharatiya Janata Party. We extend our warm congratulations to all the dedicated workers and office-bearers of the BJP for this victory.In Bapni Pur and Datia, we did not receive the expected mandate. We will conduct a thorough introspection of the election results in both these areas with complete seriousness, and with renewed energy and determination, we will continue to go among the people and work tirelessly to further strengthen their trust."Bankipur had been one of the BJP's strongest urban bastions since 1995. The seat was represented first by BJP leader Navin Kishore Prasad Sinha and later by his son, Nitin Nabin, who held it for five consecutive terms before vacating it after his election to the Rajya Sabha, triggering the bypoll.In the 2025 Bihar Assembly election, Nabin had retained the seat by a margin of more than 50,000 votes, making Kishor's victory one of the biggest political upsets in the state ahead of the Assembly elections.The bypoll also marked Prashant Kishor's electoral debut. After years as a political strategist, he launched the Jan Suraaj Party with a campaign centred on education, employment and governance reforms. His victory gives the fledgling party its first electoral success.Earlier in the day, Kishor said the result carried a message beyond Bankipur."It was an attempt by the people of Bihar to send a message to the BJP's central leadership that they should appoint a good person as the Chief Minister of Bihar," he told reporters.Following the result, the Jan Suraaj Party posted on X, "In democracy, the fortress belongs only to the people. Thank you, Bankipur--this is your victory."Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary also congratulated Kishor on his victory."In the grand festival of democracy, the people have chosen Jan Suraaj in the Bankipur Assembly by-election. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to Shri Prashant Kishor ji on his victory, while respecting the people's decision," he said in a post on X.According to the Election Commission, the Bankipur bypoll recorded a voter turnout of 34.24 per cent.
Article Summary: BJP national president Nitin Nabin says party will undertake a "thorough introspection" after losing Bankipur bypoll. Jan Suraaj founder Prashant Kishor defeated BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar to end the party's three-decade dominance in the constituency.

Article Title: Russian drone chases Ukrainian vegetable seller in 'safari' attack - Watch
Article Text:
Russian drone targets Ukrainian vegetable seller in 'Safari' attack

Ukraine on Tuesday accused Russia of committing a war crime after footage emerged showing a Russian drone pursuing and striking a vegetable seller in the southern city of Kherson, leaving the civilian wounded.Video footage shows a drone pursuing a man around a van being used as a roadside vegetable stall before exploding as he dives behind the vehicle for cover. Police said the man, in his 50s, survived the attack but sustained shrapnel injuries and suffered shock.Reacting to the incident, Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the latest footage highlighted what he described as Russia's continued targeting of civilians in Kherson."Today, many were shocked by yet another video of the drone 'safari' Russians are carrying out against civilians in Kherson," Zelenskyy said in a post on X, adding that "Russia has gone mad" and calling for increased pressure on Moscow and strong security guarantees for Ukraine."The world must see this. It must see every piece of evidence that Russia has gone mad and that its soldiers take pleasure in killing and abusing civilians.Without pressure on Russia, the dismantling of its capacity for aggression, and real security guarantees, it is simply impossible to imagine the world being able to coexist with this evil. We must remain resolute in defending life. We must act and support life in ways that force Russia to seriously think about peace rather than expanding the range of its drones," Zelenskyy added.Ukrainian authorities later identified the victim only as 52-year-old Yurii and released a video interview with him from the hospital.According to Oleksandr Prokudin head of the Kherson regional military administration, Yurii had travelled to Kherson that morning to sell vegetables. Prokudin shared the hospital interview on Telegram.Yurii said he and his wife were arranging crates of vegetables beside their van when he heard the distinctive buzz of a drone overhead. As his wife fled, he said, the drone turned its attention to him. He recalled holding up several heads of garlic toward the drone's camera to signal to its operator that he was not filming it."It could see that I had tomatoes out, some cucumbers and eggplants laid out on the floor," Yurii said, as cited by the BBC. "It even ducked under the umbrella when I was running away round the other side."So-called "safari" attacks, in which drones are allegedly used to hunt civilians, have been reported in Kherson for months. The southern city lies just a few miles from the front line.A 2025 United Nations report said it found that Russian armed forces had "recurrently killed and injured civilians" in the area by using drones to target them.Ukraine has also carried out drone and long-range missile strikes inside Russia, which Russian authorities say have resulted in civilian casualties.Russia on Monday accused Ukraine of carrying out a "terrorist" attack after seven people, including three children, were killed at the Black Sea resort town of Gelendzhik in what Moscow described as a deliberate drone strike targeting civilians.
Article Summary: Video footage shows a drone pursuing a man around a van being used as a roadside vegetable stall. Police said the man, in his 50s, survived the attack but sustained shrapnel injuries and suffered shock. Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the latest footage highlighted what he described as Russia's continued targeting of civilians.

Article Title: Man arrested with gun, ammunition near Trump's California golf course ahead of fundraiser
Article Text:
Armed man held near Trump golf course after allegedly monitoring security preparations

A 38-year-old man was arrested near President Donald Trump's Los Angeles-area golf course after authorities alleged he was monitoring security preparations ahead of Trump's fundraising event at the venue, the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department said.The man, identified as Jeanine John Taele, was detained on Sunday after deputies found a 16-round magazine with ammunition in his pocket. Authorities also recovered a loaded pistol from his vehicle. Investigators later searched his home in the nearby city of Downey and seized multiple firearms, magazines, ammunition, body armour and notebooks containing what officials described as "concerning statements."The arrest was announced as Trump prepared to attend a fundraising dinner for the Republican National Committee at Trump National Golf Course in Rancho Palos Verdes, south of Los Angeles.According to the sheriff's department, Taele had been taking photographs and recording videos around the golf course while appearing to monitor security arrangements two days before the event.Taele has been charged with several felony offences, including second-degree robbery, receiving a large-capacity magazine and possession of a short-barrelled rifle or shotgun.He also faces a misdemeanor charge of carrying a concealed firearm in a vehicle.He pleaded not guilty to all charges on Monday. A court ordered him to stay away from the golf course and prohibited him from possessing weapons. His bail was set at $250,000.Authorities said Taele was already under investigation by the El Segundo Police Department in connection with a robbery case when deputies contacted him on Sunday.The sheriff's department said there is "no credible threat to our communities."The arrest comes more than a year after a jury in 2025 found a man guilty of attempting to assassinate Trump at the president's Florida golf club.
Article Summary: Man, identified as Jeanine John Taele, was detained on Sunday after deputies found a 16-round magazine with ammunition in his pocket. Authorities recovered a loaded pistol from his vehicle. Investigators later searched his home in the nearby city of Downey and seized multiple firearms, magazines, ammunition, body armour and notebooks.

Article Title: Russia-Ukraine war intensifies: Overnight airstrikes kill 14 in Kyiv, damage warehouses, spark fire - watch
Article Text:
Footage of the explosion caused by the airstrikes (Photo: X/ @AMK_Mapping)​

Russian airstrikes on the Ukrainian capital Kyiv killed 14 early on Wednesday morning amid increased attacks on the capital. 27 others were injured as buildings and warehouses got damaged in a massive fire triggered by the strikes. The capital city of Ukraine experienced air raid alerts for over an hour and seven military sites were struck in an assault that began after midnight.Mayor Vitali Klitschko informed that one warehouse building had been destroyed near the city centre and rescue teams had pulled two people from the ruins.“There may still be people under the rubble”, he wrote on Telegram, adding that search and rescue operations are proceeding, with an ambulance driver being among the injured.Additionally, the city’s military administration said the assault caused an ammonia leak, which was being tackled by emergency crews.According to AFP, journalists heard explosions in Kyiv after midnight following a warning from the Ukrainian air force about incoming ballistic missiles.Kyiv’s military administration said the barrage damaged residential buildings and several warehouses.Earlier, Russian attacks on Saturday had killed 10 people and injured more than 30, while Ukrainian drones sank a large Russian container ship in the Black Sea.As Russia increases its use of ballistic missiles, Ukraine has urged its allies to provide more US-made Patriot interceptors.Both sides have stepped up long-range attacks in recent weeks. Russia more than doubled its use of missiles in July, according to an AFP analysis.Drone attacks have also become a regular occurrence, with Ukraine intensifying strikes on civilian infrastructure, including oil and gas facilities and logistics sites in Russia.On Tuesday morning, five people were killed, and 10 others were injured in the Moscow region as Ukraine targeted depots belonging to Russian e-commerce giant Wildberries, AFP reported.Moscow’s mayor said on Wednesday that Russian air defences had intercepted and destroyed at least 10 drones heading towards the capital.Meanwhile, Ukraine expressed outrage over a video showing a man being chased by a drone in the battle-struck city of Kherson, describing it as a deliberate “hunt” and “safari” targeting civilians.United Nations human rights monitors have raised concerns over the rising number of civilian casualties, which have reached their highest level since the war began in February 2022.
Article Summary: Russian airstrikes on the Ukrainian capital Kyiv killed 14 early on Wednesday morning. 27 others were injured as buildings and warehouses got damaged in a massive fire triggered by the strikes. The capital city of Ukraine experienced air raid alerts for over an hour and seven military sites were struck.

Article Title: NOC to travel outside Islamabad, Lahore, Karachi - Pakistan restricts foreign journalists amid PoK crackdown
Article Text:
Pakistan tightens curbs on foreign media (Reuters image)

Pakistan has imposed fresh restrictions on foreign media personnel, requiring journalists working for international news organisations to obtain a No Objection Certificate (NOC) before travelling outside Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi for reporting assignments.The new guidelines, issued by Pakistan's ministry of information and broadcasting (MoIB), establish a comprehensive framework governing the registration, accreditation and movement of foreign media organisations and journalists operating in the country.Under the rules, journalists are exempt from the No Objection Certificate (NOC) requirement when travelling within Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi. For personal travel to Abbottabad and Murree, they may apply for an NOC through the ministry's External Publicity (EP) Wing, with approvals expected within three working days.“All Pakistani journalists residing abroad, contributing to foreign media and seeking registration must submit their application through the EP Wing portal and concurrently forward their case through the nearest press attaché, counsellor, minister posted in Pakistan missions, consulates, high commissions, or embassies,” the MOIB said, as cited by Dawn.Additionally, the guidelines require all companies, entities, production houses and other organisations operating in Pakistan to facilitate foreign media "in any capacity" to register with the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting's publicity wing.The registration requirement also applies to non-journalists residing in Pakistan who provide services to foreign media organisations.The new rules apply to all international media organisations, including print, electronic and digital outlets, as well as web-based platforms and social media organisations.The regulations also require production houses, companies, freelancers, fixers and non-journalists providing services to foreign media in Pakistan to register with the ministry. It clarified that the registration is intended solely for professional recognition and does not grant any official status."All foreign/international media personnel already accredited or registered with EP Wing shall be required a mandatory NOC from EP Wing for movement to any other city (except Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi) in case they are going to produce a news content, story, video, film, documentary or social media content for their official use," the guidelines state.After completing the registration process, journalists seeking a press accreditation card must submit an application through the online portal along with the required documents. The guidelines provide for two categories of accreditation: permanent accreditation, issued annually, and temporary accreditation for visiting journalists, valid for up to three months.Once the external publicity wing issues the accreditation card, it will "facilitate" journalists' access to official media events and government premises.The guidelines state that journalists will be "bound to produce that card on demand", and must surrender it if they change their organisation or accreditation category, or when the accreditation period expires.The latest measures come amid heightened scrutiny of media access in Pakistan following reports of protests, disruptions and the alleged use of force during the local election process in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoK).Human rights and press freedom organisations, including Amnesty International and Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ), have raised concerns over alleged restrictions on journalists, communication blackouts, enforced disappearances of media personnel and curbs on foreign media coverage of the protests. Amnesty International has also called for an independent investigation into allegations of excessive force used against demonstrators in Rawalakot.
Article Summary: New guidelines establish framework governing registration, accreditation and movement of foreign media. Journalists exempt from NOC requirement when travelling within Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi. For personal travel to Abbottabad and Murree, they may apply for NOC through ministry's External Publicity (EP) Wing.

Article Title: 'We'll know in 48 hours': Trump warns Iran to open Hormuz or get 'hit very hard'
Article Text:
US, Iran and Oman near interim deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz. Trump warns Tehran to reach a deal soon.

US president Donald Trump has signalled that a possible breakthrough in talks with Iran could come within 48 hours, while warning Tehran that the Strait of Hormuz must reopen “very soon” as part of a deal with Iran and Oman, or face military action.Speaking to reporters in California on Tuesday, Trump said negotiations with Iran were “moving along very nicely”. “We’ll find out. We’ll know in 48 hours,” he added.The comments came as Axios reported that the US, Iran and Oman were nearing an interim agreement aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz, with Washington hoping for an announcement on Wednesday.The remarks came after Trump told Fox News that the two sides had held an “all-day negotiation”. The US president described the discussions positively while warning Iran could be hit “really hard” if a deal was not reached.“They had an all-day negotiation,” Trump told Fox News, adding, “We are having very good discussions."In an interview with Fox News, Trump linked the negotiations directly to the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.“The strait is going to be open very soon, or they’re going to get hit very hard – and then the strait’s going to be open,” Trump said.Trump also said Washington and Tehran were engaged in “very good discussions”, despite repeated Iranian denials of direct talks. “They don’t like to admit that, but yeah, it’s a little bit disconcerting,” he said.“The only thing that matters is action, and they want to make a deal. We’ll see what happens. If they don’t make a deal, it’s going to be too bad,” he added.Trump also reiterated that Iran would never have a nuclear weapon. "They already can't, but they'll--it's going to be formal. The strait's going to be open very soon, or they're going to get hit very hard, and then the strait's going to be open", he added.Trump said Washington had been preparing a major military operation against Iran before diplomacy took precedence after Tehran sought talks.“We were going into a tremendous attack, the biggest since World War II, and they called me and said, very politely, 'Please, can we talk? Can we talk?'” Trump told Fox News. “Yes, we can talk. Let's get it done.”Trump on Saturday postponed large-scale strikes against Iran after consultations with Gulf partners, giving diplomatic efforts more time.
Article Summary: US, Iran and Oman near interim deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz. Trump warns Tehran to reach a deal soon. Comments came as Axios reported that the US, Iran. and Oman were nearing an interim agreement aimed at reopening the Strait of. Hormuez.

Article Title: What is 'Operation Fortress'? Reform UK's military plan to stop migrants crossing English Channel
Article Text:
Reform UK leader Nigel Farage unveiled 'Operation Fortress'.

What is Operation Fortress?

Ceuta crisis cited as warning for Europe

Experts question feasibility

Why is Reform UK pushing the plan now?

Britain and France already have migration pact

Britain's right-wing Reform UK party has unveiled 'Operation Fortress', a military-led plan that it says would end illegal migrant crossings across the English Channel if it comes to power.Party leader Nigel Farage described it as the "largest military operation in the Channel since World War II," promising to deploy the Royal Navy to intercept small boats and return migrants to France.Under the proposed policy, the Royal Navy would be tasked with intercepting migrant boats attempting to cross the English Channel and escorting them back to France. Reform UK claims the operation would make Britain's borders "impenetrable" and end small-boat crossings within weeks."Under a Reform government, within a fortnight, there would be no more boats," Farage said while unveiling the plan.Announcing the proposal on Monday, Farage pointed to the recent migrant surge in Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta, saying the crisis highlighted the rising challenge of irregular migration across Europe.Last week, thousands of migrants attempted to enter Ceuta from neighbouring Morocco, putting fresh pressure on Spanish authorities and reigniting the debate over Europe's border security.Reform UK argued that Britain must act before facing a similar situation, using the developments in Ceuta as justification for its tougher border strategy.The proposal, however, drew immediate criticism from military experts and political opponents, who questioned both its legality and practicality.Andrew Fox, a former British paratrooper and senior associate fellow at the Henry Jackson Society think tank, said the plan overlooked key legal and operational hurdles, news agency Reuters reported.According to Fox, British warships cannot enter French territorial waters, seize migrant boats or disembark passengers in France without Paris' consent.Former Royal Navy commander Tom Sharpe also dismissed the proposal, saying naval vessels are not designed to function as "passenger ferries" and cannot simply return migrants against France's wishes.The announcement comes as Reform UK faces scrutiny over donations and financial disclosures involving senior party figures, with recent opinion polls showing the party losing its lead after more than a year.Labour accused Reform of recycling old immigration proposals to divert attention from questions over its finances.Meanwhile, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has also vowed "relentless" action to curb small-boat crossings after more than 2,000 migrants reportedly arrived in Britain during the first two weeks of his premiership.Britain and France signed a three-year agreement earlier this year under which London will provide up to 766 million euros to help France strengthen efforts to prevent small-boat crossings across the Channel.Despite those measures, migration remains one of Britain's most controversial political issues, with thousands continuing to attempt the dangerous sea crossing each year.
Article Summary: Reform UK party unveils plan to intercept small boats and return migrants to France. Party leader Nigel Farage says it would make Britain's borders "impenetrable" Plan draws criticism from military experts and political opponents. Reform UK faces scrutiny over donations and financial disclosures involving senior party figures.

Article Title: What is CJP's next move? Core members to meet in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on Aug 5 to chart future course
Article Text:
(With agency inputs)





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Core members of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) will meet at founder Abhijeet Dipke's residence in Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on August 5 to discuss the outfit's future course of action, sources said on Sunday.According to news agency PTI, CJP activists and volunteers were asked to spend time with their families after the outfit's month-long agitation against the alleged NEET paper leak at Delhi's Jantar Mantar last month.The core members of the CJP were also asked to interact with volunteers and students and bring their feedback, views and suggestions to the upcoming meeting, sources said.The outfit will hold a press conference after the August 5 meeting to announce decisions on its future course of action, sources said.Meanwhile, Dipke met students, locals and visitors from neighbouring districts at his residence and celebrated Friendship Day with children.Earlier, Abhijeet Dipke urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to go beyond social media gestures and direct authorities to withdraw cases filed against student protesters."Don't just offer forgiveness on Instagram; direct the police to withdraw the cases as well. Withdraw the cases filed against these students," Dipke told ANI.Demanding a formal apology over the police action against students on July 20, Dipke said the Prime Minister's "forgiveness" could not be discussed unless the government first acknowledged the alleged "brutality" faced by the protesters."PM Modi should apologise to the students who were subjected to a lathicharge on July 20, those who suffered head injuries, pellet gun wounds, and serious injuries such as broken arms and legs. Apologise to them first; only then can you talk about forgiveness," he said.The CJP-led protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar over the alleged NEET paper leak scandal received widespread support from Gen Z across the country, eventually leading to Union Education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation last week.
Article Summary: Core members of Cockroach Janta Party will meet at founder Abhijeet Dipke's residence in Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on August 5. CJP activists and volunteers were asked to spend time with their families after the outfit's month-long agitation against the alleged NEET paper leak.

Article Title: Clavicular’s legal case takes unexpected turn after prosecutors make surprise decision over alleged ‘instigated’ Airbnb fight
Article Text:
Clavicular’s legal case takes unexpected turn after prosecutors make surprise decision over alleged ‘instigated’ Airbnb fight

Why prosecutors dropped the case against Braden Eric Peters, known as Clavicular

What the Osceola County Sheriff’s Department said about the investigation

Influencer and streamer Clavicular will not face criminal charges over his alleged role in a fight between two women at a Florida short-term rental. Prosecutors have dismissed the misdemeanor battery case, bringing the legal matter to an end for now. The decision came months after Clavicular, whose real name is Braden Eric Peters, was arrested in March following an investigation into a February incident. According to TMZ, prosecutors decided to drop the case because they could not prove the charge beyond a reasonable doubt, based on court documents cited by local news outlets.The case began after authorities accused Clavicular of encouraging two women to get into a physical fight at an Airbnb-style rental property in Florida. Investigators also alleged that he later shared a video of the incident on social media to gain attention.Clavicular was arrested in March on a warrant from Osceola County and was charged with misdemeanor battery. However, that charge will no longer move forward.According to court documents cited by local news outlets, prosecutors dismissed the case because they could not prove the allegation beyond a reasonable doubt.That legal standard requires prosecutors to present enough evidence to convince a jury of a defendant’s guilt. In this case, they decided they could not meet that burden, leading to the dismissal of the charge.While prosecutors decided not to continue the case, the Osceola County Sheriff’s Department had earlier shared a different view during its investigation.The department said detectives believed Clavicular “instigated” a fight between two women and later posted it on social media to “exploit” them. Those allegations formed the basis of the investigation that eventually led to his arrest.Even so, an investigation by law enforcement and a criminal prosecution are separate processes. Although detectives believed there was enough reason to make an arrest, prosecutors later concluded they did not have enough evidence to secure a conviction in court.With the case now dismissed, Clavicular is no longer facing criminal prosecution over the February incident. The dismissal does not mean the allegations were proven or disproven. It means prosecutors determined the available evidence was not strong enough to meet the legal standard required for a criminal conviction.The decision closes the criminal case that began earlier this year after the fight at the Florida rental property and the video that followed.
Article Summary: Influencer and streamer Clavicular will not face criminal charges over his alleged role in a fight between two women at a Florida short-term rental. Prosecutors decided to drop the case because they could not prove the charge beyond a reasonable doubt, according to court documents. The case began after authorities accused him of encouraging two women to get into a physical fight at an Airbnb-style rental property in Florida.

Article Title: Why does Asmongold want Twitch to be sued? Here’s what he said, “Because they have created an…”
Article Text:
Why does Asmongold want Twitch to be sued? Here’s what he said, “Because they have created an…”

Why Asmongold believes Twitch should be held responsible for distracted driving streams

Twitch’s driving stream rules remain under scrutiny

As driving livestreams continue to spark safety concerns, popular streamer Asmongold has now gone a step further by saying Twitch should face legal action if someone is killed because of distracted driving during a broadcast. Speaking after a viral clip showed a streamer apparently sleeping behind the wheel, he argued that the platform is doing more than simply hosting the content. According to Asmongold, Twitch has created a system that rewards these streams, even after repeated warnings about the risks. His comments have once again put the spotlight on how the platform handles driving-related content.Asmongold shared his views during a livestream on August 3, reacting to a clip that had spread online showing a streamer seemingly asleep while driving.“I can’t wait for one of these streamers to kill somebody on stream because of distracted driving. I want Twitch to get sued,” Asmongold said, adding that it is “crazy” that people still have “leeway” for driving streams.He then explained why he believes the platform should also be held responsible if a serious accident happens.“Why would Twitch get sued for that? Because they have created an incentive structure around allowing people to distracted drive on their platform that they’ve profited from, they’ve been made away of this, and they’ve chosen to ignore it.“And, by choosing to ignore it and allowing paying and incentivizing people to continue doing distracted driving, they’ve now created more of this distracted driving, which I think means they are partially liable for the behavior of people that are doing this.”His comments came as the debate around livestreaming while driving continues to grow. The issue has drawn criticism from several creators who believe broadcasting from behind the wheel puts both streamers and others on the road at risk.Driving streams have been part of Twitch for years, but they have faced heavier criticism in recent months after several incidents where streamers appeared distracted while driving.Twitch has already updated its rules around driving broadcasts. Under the platform’s policy, streamers are not allowed to respond to chat, touch their phones or engage in other behavior that could distract them while driving. Those who break the rules can face suspensions, although many of those bans have only lasted a short time.Even with those changes, some creators believe the rules do not go far enough. Asmongold has previously called for driving streams to be banned completely. He has also suggested that streamers should use ride-sharing services or hire personal drivers if they want to broadcast while travelling.Streamer DansGaming has also spoken against the trend, saying, “Drivers are terrible and dangerous enough when they aren’t streaming. This should never be encouraged or allowed on Twitch.”
Article Summary: Streamer Asmongold says Twitch should face legal action if someone is killed during a broadcast. He believes the platform has created an incentive system that rewards distracted driving. His comments come as the debate around livestreaming while driving continues to grow. Twitch has already updated its rules around driving broadcasts.
